title: Iris Zero
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a world where 99% of young people have an eye power called an Iris, Toru Mizushima is one of the few with none, and after being shunned as a child he lives by a motto of 'minimal exposure.' When popular Koyuki Sasamori asks for his help, he starts using reason and observation to solve classmates' problems, gaining friends while facing jealousy and prejudice.
life_message: Insight, honesty and care can matter more than special gifts, and outsiders deserve a place among friends.

content.note: MU Serial Killer/s; a friend's Iris foresees death and Toru helps prevent a murder (Wikipedia); a slap of a counselor.
Mystery incidents and premonitions of death.
Slow school romance between Toru and Koyuki (MU Slow Romance); MangaDex safe.
Childhood shunning and bullying; a classmate is saved from killing herself (Wikipedia); MU Self-Harm, Bullying, Childhood Trauma.
Bullying and psychological manipulation of peers (Kuga's arc) shown as harmful.

dominant: Reason and empathy; inclusion of outsiders; friendship

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts resolved by reasoning and explanation, not retaliation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: School order and student council matter; minimal exposure as conformity.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Classmates and friends, not family, are the circle.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Critiques ranking people by Iris ability.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Rational deduction is the hero's tool.

folkways.japan: Toru's 'minimal exposure' motto reflects Japanese school pressures to avoid standing out (the nail that sticks up gets hammered down).

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia summaries show themes carried by case-by-case character arcs; no review on delivery found (to verify).

personified.ideology: Reason and empathy over innate privilege

delivery.note: Prejudice against the powerless is shown through classmates who later reconcile, rather than through one-note villains.

winners_losers: Toru and his growing circle win; prejudiced classmates are mostly redeemed rather than punished.
